questions.question: Motorcycles are allowed to:

options.text: Use a full lane without sharing it.
Share a lane with a car.
Share a lane with a small truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a full lane without sharing it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use a full traffic lane. Other drivers cannot drive in a way that takes away this right.

questions.question: As your motorcycle goes faster, you will:

options.text: Need to shift up through the gears.
Need to shift down through the gears.
Need to put the motorcycle into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need to shift up through the gears.
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle speeds up, you must shift into higher gears.

questions.question: The best way to stop quickly is to:

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both the front and rear brakes at the same time with steady pressure.

questions.question: Pick a lane position that:

options.text: Places you directly next to another vehicle.

questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you avoid road hazards. Keep safe space around your motorcycle at all times.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It has white with red and black markings. This sign means U-turns are not allowed in this area.

questions.question: When approaching an uneven surface, such as a bump or pothole, you should rise slightly off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off the motorcycle if needed.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can get a better view of the uneven surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: When you rise off your seat over uneven surfaces, your legs and joints absorb some of the impact. This helps keep you on the motorcycle.

questions.question: A benefit of keeping space between you and surrounding vehicles is that:

options.text: You can draft off other vehicles better.
You have more time to react to what other drivers do.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: Keep safe space around your motorcycle. This gives you more time to see and respond to dangers. You also have more room to move safely if needed.

questions.question: Pick a lane position that:

options.text: Makes you more visible and keeps safe space around you.
You like, without thinking about others.
Gets you close to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes you more visible and keeps safe space around you.
questions.explanation: Position yourself where other drivers can see you best. Keep safe space around your motorcycle. Good riders change their position as road conditions change. No single position is always best or always bad.

questions.question: Use your mirrors when stopping at an intersection to:

options.text: See if drivers behind you know you are stopping.
Look for dark clouds that may mean bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: See if drivers behind you know you are stopping.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when you stop. This tells you if drivers behind you see you and are responding to your stop. Make sure they are paying attention to you.

questions.question: To reduce fatigue while riding, you should:
questions.explanation: Take breaks often during long rides to fight fatigue. Caffeine and other stimulants can make fatigue worse when they wear off. Dress warmly and use a windshield on long rides to stay comfortable and alert.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Ride at the same speed as during the day.
Ride slower than you would during the day.
Ride faster than you would during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than you would during the day.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night, especially on unfamiliar roads. Slower speeds give you more time to spot and avoid hazards when visibility is poor.

questions.question: Before riding, a motorcycle operator should check the throttle. It should:
questions.explanation: Check your throttle before riding. The throttle should snap back when you release it. Your clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because:

options.text: The front tire affects steering, which affects your balance.
A flat front tire will stop the front brake from working.
A flat front tire will prevent acceleration.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front tire affects steering, which affects your balance.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it makes steering hard, which makes it hard to keep your balance. If steering feels heavy, you may have a flat front tire.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT recommended as protective gear for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Wear protective gear when riding. Good protective gear includes long-sleeved jackets, long heavy pants, closed-toe boots that cover your ankles, and full-fingered leather gloves. Cover as much skin as possible.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is coming up.

questions.question: When entering a turn, you should:

options.text: Take the motorcycle out of gear.

questions.explanation: Change gears before you start a turn. If you must change gears while turning, do it smoothly.

questions.question: What removes alcohol from a person's body?
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Nothing else can speed up this process.

questions.question: The best way to handle tailgaters is usually to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let tailgaters pass. Riding faster may increase danger by encouraging them to keep tailgating at the higher speed.

questions.question: Riding right after rain starts is difficult because:

options.text: Other drivers may not react fast enough to the rain.
Other drivers drive too slowly in wet weather.

questions.explanation: The pavement is very slippery right after rain starts. Oil from vehicles has not yet washed away, creating a slippery layer when mixed with water.

questions.question: To work well, an eye or face shield must:

options.text: Limit side vision so you focus on the road ahead.
Not allow eyeglasses or sunglasses to be worn.

questions.explanation: An effective eye or face shield must be scratch-free, hard to break, allow clear views to the sides, fasten securely, let air flow through to prevent fogging, and allow room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: You may go through the intersection carefully.
You must let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. Stop your vehicle completely and wait for a green signal before turning in that direction.

questions.question: Where should a passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: To the side of the seat.

questions.explanation: A passenger must sit behind the rider and hold tightly to the rider's waist or hips. The passenger can also hold onto handgrips if the motorcycle has them. Never sit to the side of the seat.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?
questions.explanation: Dry pavement gives the best grip. Wet roads, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates can reduce tire grip and are dangerous for motorcycles.

questions.question: What should NOT be included in a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, controls, lights, signals, mirrors, brakes, oil, fluids, frame, and stands. Paint inspection is not part of a safety check.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes to let them pass, or slow down to increase the space ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to let them pass, or slow down to increase the space ahead of you.
questions.explanation: Let the tailgater pass safely. Going faster will only make them follow you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: Which material protects motorcycle riders the best?
questions.explanation: Leather and tough synthetic materials offer the best protection for riders in a crash.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of vehicles moving slower than 25 mph, like farm equipment, construction vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: What should you do before riding a borrowed motorcycle?

options.text: Assume the controls are in the same place as your motorcycle.
Take it straight out on the highway.
Practice with it in a safe, quiet area first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice with it in a safe, quiet area first.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Learn where all the controls are on a new motorcycle. Practice in a quiet area before riding on the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert you to road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic is merging into your lane.

questions.question: What is most important when buying a motorcycle helmet?
questions.explanation: Protection should be your main concern. Choose a helmet that fits snugly, fastens securely, and has a DOT safety rating.
